domain_calc.description: Refrigerant saturation math from CoolProp tables: pt_lookup, superheat (dew point), subcool (bubble point). 'pt_lookup' gives the dew and bubble saturation temperatures at a gauge pressure, or the saturation pressures at a temperature. 'superheat' is suction line temperature minus the dew-point temperature at suction pressure; 'subcool' is the bubble-point temperature at liquid pressure minus liquid line temperature. Pressures in psig (answer in °F) or kPa/bar gauge (answer in °C and K). Gauge pressure assumes sea level unless altitude_ft or altitude_m is given. Never assume the refrigerant: take it from the nameplate or ask. Use superheat/subcool for values the technician says when refrigerant_gauges has no usable picture: a pressure implausible for the refrigerant is asked again, and with a job open the spoken pressure and line temperature are recorded. 'voltage_drop' (electrical): the drop along a run from 'phase' ('single' or 'three'), 'current_a', the one-way length ('length_m' or 'length_ft') and the conductor: 'wire_awg' with 'material' is enough, or a resistance per unit length ('resistance_ohm_per_km', '_per_m', '_per_1000ft' or '_per_ft'), or a factor with the area ('k_factor_ohm_mm2_per_m' with 'area_mm2', or 'k_factor_ohm_cmil_per_ft' with 'area_cmil'), which win over the gauge; 'supply_v' adds the drop as a percentage. A resistance or factor comes from the technician or the organisation's own book, never from memory; never assume the phase, the material or a resistance.

altitude_ft.description: Optional site altitude (feet) to correct gauge pressure for local atmosphere.

altitude_m.description: Optional site altitude (metres) to correct gauge pressure for local atmosphere.

application.description: For 'superheat'/'subcool', what the system is doing if the technician said: comfort cooling, heat pump heating, or refrigeration. Narrows the plausibility check.

area_cmil.description: For 'voltage_drop': the conductor's area (circular mils), with 'k_factor_ohm_cmil_per_ft'.

current_a.description: For 'voltage_drop': the current the run carries (A).

k_factor_ohm_cmil_per_ft.description: For 'voltage_drop' instead of a resistance: the factor (Ω·cmil/ft), with 'area_cmil'.

k_factor_ohm_mm2_per_m.description: For 'voltage_drop' instead of a resistance: the factor (Ω·mm²/m), with 'area_mm2'.

material.description: For 'voltage_drop' with 'wire_awg': the conductor's metal. Never assumed.

phase.description: For 'voltage_drop': a single-phase or a three-phase run. Never assumed.

pressure_reference.description: 'gauge' (default) or 'absolute' when the instrument reads absolute (psia, kPa abs, bar abs).

refrigerant.description: Refrigerant designation, from the nameplate or the technician: R-22, R-32, R-134a, R-404A, R-407A, R-407C, R-410A, R-454B, R-507A, R-290, R-600a, R-744, R-1234yf.

refrigerant_source.description: Where 'refrigerant' came from: the nameplate, the technician, or the unit's display. Default 'technician'.

supply_v.description: For 'voltage_drop': the supply voltage, for the drop as a percentage.

temperature_c.description: For 'pt_lookup' instead of a pressure: a saturation temperature (°C); answers in kPa(g).

temperature_f.description: For 'pt_lookup' instead of a pressure: a saturation temperature (°F); answers in psig.

wire_awg.description: For 'voltage_drop': the wire's AWG size ('14', '1/0'), with 'material'. Enough without a resistance or area.

equipment_lookup.description: Look up an equipment error code, fault, or model number in the active Field Assist vault. The technician can read the code/model aloud (pass 'query'), or point the camera (the glasses when connected, otherwise the phone) at the nameplate / error display and omit 'query' (or set 'use_camera') to read it via on-device OCR. Returns the matching reference section with its source file. Use before diagnosing so the answer is grounded. When a lookup or a nameplate read names exactly one model the vault covers, that model becomes the session's active equipment and every later answer is scoped to it — say so to the technician. Pass 'set_equipment' with a model or part of one to correct a wrong read ("no, it's the 070"), or to record the model the technician says the unit in front of them is — including one the manuals do not cover, which is still recorded as said. Pass 'serial' (and/or 'field_name' + 'field_value' for another nameplate field) when the technician reads one out, so the record keeps it. Use 'clear_equipment' to forget the unit. Requires an active session.

field_name.description: Another nameplate field the technician read out (e.g. 'firmware', 'refrigerant'). Pass with field_value.

field_value.description: The value of field_name, exactly as read.

file.description: Optional: restrict the search to a single vault file (e.g. 'error_codes.md').

query.description: The error code, fault, or model to look up (e.g. 'E5', 'Carrier 30RB'). Omit to read it from the camera.

serial.description: The unit's serial number, exactly as the technician read it out.

set_equipment.description: Set the session's active equipment to this model (a full model number or part of one, e.g. '070'). Use when the technician corrects a nameplate read.

use_camera.description: Force reading the code/model from the camera via OCR even if a query is given.

evidence.description: Choose which of the open job's photos and clips go with its report. 'exclude' or 'include' with 'item' 'latest' (the default) or an item id: "leave that photo out", "put the last picture back". 'keep' records that the technician wants them sent as they are, 'include_all' and 'exclude_all' do what they say. The choice is kept whether or not the close review happens. Requires an active session.

item.description: 'latest' (default) or the id of one photo or clip.

field_session.description: Start, pause, resume, end, update, or query a Field Assist session for grounded, domain-specific technical support including installed custom vaults. Sessions load a knowledge vault and emit an audit log. Use 'start' when the technician begins work on equipment, 'set_job_reference' whenever the technician gives or corrects a job/work-order number, 'set_job_details' when they name or rename the open job ("call it…", "name it…", "the job name is…"), and 'end' only when they say to end, close, finish or cancel the job. Only confirm that a job reference was recorded after this tool action succeeds. Use 'recall' to retrieve older technician reports, readings and task results for the current equipment when they are absent from the working context. Reports are not independently verified. Read subsequent records for corrections; paginate until the relevant record is complete. For the user's default vault, omit vault or use 'default'. Use 'vaults' to discover installed vault IDs, names and the configured default. Never substitute another vault after a failure without the user's choice. An equipment/asset name does not select its knowledge vault. The default applies to new jobs only, and an open job keeps its vault: never end a job to change its vault or its name — ask the technician; a different vault applies to their next job. 'next_unit' when the technician moves to another machine on the same job ("next unit", "now the second furnace") — pass 'unit' with its model if they say it, as said; work from then on is recorded against that unit. 'separate_earlier_work' when the technician says work done before the first unit was identified was on a different machine ("that was a different unit", "the earlier work was on the other furnace"): the earlier work stays on an unidentified unit of its own and the identified machine becomes a separate unit. Only after an identification reply said earlier work was attached to it. Jobs ahead: 'add_upcoming_job' records a job the technician describes before going there ("next job: 1007, no heat, Smith Street") — pass only the fields they actually said, word for word, and never fill one in; 'brief_next_job' has the app read the cited brief aloud; 'brief_more' reads one section of it in full. For directions to it, use get_directions with next_job.

action.description: Action: 'start' to begin a new session, 'set_job_reference' to record or correct its job/work-order number, 'set_job_details' to name or rename the open job (and optionally its job_reference), 'next_unit' to move to another machine on the same job, 'separate_earlier_work' when work recorded before the first identification was on a different machine, 'pause' to pause billing, 'resume' to continue, 'end' to finish (only when the technician asks to end, close, finish or cancel the job), 'status' to query the active session, 'list' for history, 'recall' for older current-equipment records, 'vaults' for installed vault IDs/names and the configured default, 'escalate' to flag the session for a human expert (only when the technician asks for a person or says yes to your offer), 'export' to produce a work-order PDF + audit JSON, 'add_upcoming_job' to record a job ahead, 'brief_next_job' to have the app read the next job's brief aloud, 'brief_more' to read one section of it in full.

address.description: On add_upcoming_job: the site address, exactly as said. Never looked up or completed.

contact.description: On add_upcoming_job: the site contact, exactly as said.

customer.description: On add_upcoming_job: the customer's name, exactly as said.

fault_report.description: On add_upcoming_job: the fault as the technician relayed it ("no heat, showing E200"), verbatim.

format.description: On 'export': 'pdf', 'json', or 'both' (default). 'pdf' is the customer-facing work order; 'json' is the structured audit record.

job_reference.description: The technician's exact job or work-order number. Required on 'set_job_reference'; optional on 'set_job_details', and on 'start' when they already said it ("start job 1005"). Pass only a number they actually gave. Do not invent or normalize it, and never take it from an asset id.

mode.description: Session mode: 'ai_only' (default) or 'human_assisted' (requires expert escalation infra; reserved).

model.description: On add_upcoming_job: a machine model they named. Omit unless said.

name.description: On 'set_job_details': the job's name, exactly as the technician said it.

notes.description: On add_upcoming_job: anything else they asked to note.

offset.description: On recall: character offset from the previous page's continuation, default 0. Keep the same query.

query.description: On recall: phrase or source ID to find. Empty retrieves all current-equipment records chronologically.

reason.description: On 'escalate': human-readable reason for the escalation.

section.description: On brief_more: which part of the brief — 'site', 'equipment', 'fault', 'crew' or 'parts'.

serial.description: On add_upcoming_job: a serial number they read out. Omit unless said.

test_result.description: On 'end': what the technician said about the final test or check, in their words ("test run fine, furnace is working"). Omit when they said nothing about one.

unit.description: On next_unit: the next machine's model, exactly as the technician said it. Omit when they did not say one.

vault.description: Installed vault ID or full display name when starting. Omit or use 'default' for the configured default. Use action 'vaults' to discover choices; do not guess a generic domain instead of a custom vault.

get_datetime.description: Get the current date, time, and day of week. Optionally specify a timezone.

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier, e.g. 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'. Defaults to device timezone.

procedure_runner.description: Run a guided, step-by-step Field Assist procedure (diagnostics, checklists) within an active session. Actions: 'list' to see available procedures, 'start' to begin one, 'next' to advance (pass 'choice' to pick a branch when the active step offers choices), 'previous' to step back, 'repeat' to re-read the current step, 'status' for the current step, 'complete' to finish, 'answer' to give a step's typed answer, 'override' to take another route than a step's rule. When a step takes an answer (a reading, a choice, yes or no, a code, photos), call 'answer' with 'value' set to exactly what the technician said; the app reads and checks it, and on a step whose route follows from the answer the app decides the route, so call 'next' with no choice (a choice that disagrees with the rule is refused). A critical spoken answer is read back: say the line you get, and call 'answer' with 'confirmed' true once they agree. An out-of-spec critical answer needs a corrective note: ask what was done and pass their words as 'note'. Call 'override' only when the technician explicitly tells you to take another route, with 'branch' and their own words as 'reason'; they confirm it, and you never override a rule on your own. Reaching the last step does not finish anything: give the technician its instruction. When the last step asks for a check (a retest), pass 'confirmed' true on 'complete' only after the technician says it passed; without it the fix is recorded and a 'Verify: …' task stays open — never tell them it is resolved before then. Starting a procedure opens a task for it on the current unit. The current step and its branch choices are provided in the system prompt — use those choice ids. Coaching steps an expert sent for the job are listed and started the same way ("walk Sam's steps", "load the coaching"); read each one exactly as written.

branch.description: On 'override': the branch id the technician told you to take instead of the rule's.

choice.description: On 'next': the branch choice id for the current step (as listed in the ACTIVE PROCEDURE prompt section). Omit to follow the default path.

confirmed.description: On 'complete' at a last step that asks for a check: true only when the technician has said the check passed. On 'answer': true when the technician agrees with the read-back of their answer.

note.description: On 'answer': a corrective note, what the technician did about an out-of-spec reading, in their words.

procedure_id.description: On 'start': the procedure id (e.g. 'low_pressure_diagnostic'). Use 'list' to discover ids.

reason.description: On 'override': the technician's reason, in their own words. Required.

value.description: On 'answer': exactly what the technician said or typed for the step's answer ("4.6", "four point six", "straight", "yes"). Don't round, convert or judge it. Omit on a photo step: the photos taken on the step are attached.

reading.description: Record a value the technician reads off the machine ("supply air is 140 degrees", "inducer pressure 0.28") with 'record_reading', or correct one they gave earlier ("135, not 140") with 'correct_reading' — a correction replaces the earlier value on the record; never record it as a new reading or a task. Pass 'quantity' (what was measured), 'value' as the number alone, and 'unit' when said. Pass 'page' only for a manual page the technician confirmed. Readings are recorded as the technician's report, not as verified. Requires an active session.

action.description: Record a new reading, or correct an earlier one.

page.description: A manual page the technician confirmed this against.

quantity.description: What was measured, e.g. 'supply air', 'manifold pressure'. On correct_reading, which reading (omit for the latest).

reading_id.description: On correct_reading: the reading to correct, when known.

value.description: The number alone, without the unit, e.g. '140', '0.28'.

set_timer.description: Set a timer that will notify the user after the specified duration.

label.description: Optional label for the timer, e.g. 'pasta' or 'break time'

show_source.description: Open the manual or code-book page your last answer cited, on the technician's phone (and on glasses with a display, where it can be zoomed), with the cited passage highlighted. Call it when the technician says "show me that", "show me the page", "show me the relevant pages", "show me clause 3.9.4", "show me the table", "show me the second one" or "where does it say that": after an answer or a table_lookup it is the path that marks the row read. Pass 'which': "first" (the default), "second", "last", "all" for every cited page as one paged sheet, a clause number as printed, "table" for the table the answer cited (its row highlighted), or a table number such as "Table 99". Pass 'document' when the technician names the book. It opens only what the last answer cited, so search with manual_lookup or table_lookup and answer first. Only when the technician asks to see a page, table or source — otherwise offer it, and it opens nothing. If it reports that the phone is locked, tell the technician "It's on your phone." and do not say the page is showing. Uses your loaded manuals, or the active Field Assist session. In a personal library, name the manual when several are loaded; camera lookup requires Field Assist.

document.description: Optional: the manual or code book the technician named, by title or part of it.

which.description: Which cited source: "first", "second", "third", "last", "all", a clause number such as "3.9.4", "table", or a table number such as "Table 99".

table_lookup.description: Read one value from a table printed in the manuals or code books loaded on this phone: the cell at a row and a column, with its row and column headings, units, the notes it refers to, and the page it is printed on. Pass 'table' (its number as printed, e.g. "Table 99", or words of its title), 'row' (the row's heading, e.g. a size, a type or a range, or a number to find), and 'column' (the column's heading, e.g. "Rating group 2" or a path such as "Rating group 2 › Band B"); leave 'column' out to read the whole row. Pass 'document' when the technician names the book. If the number asked for falls between two rows it returns both rows and says so: say both, and never interpolate, round, or pick the next row yourself. If it asks which row, column, table or book, ask the technician. Read the value out as printed with its row, column and page, and repeat the Source line. A value from a table printed as a picture comes back marked "read from a picture of the table": say so, read it back for the technician to check, and offer the page, and a cell the picture did not show clearly is never given, so never supply it yourself. Uses your loaded manuals, or the active Field Assist session. In a personal library, name the manual when several are loaded; camera lookup requires Field Assist.

column.description: Optional: the column heading, or a path of headings separated by ›. Leave out to read the whole row.

document.description: Optional: the manual or code book the technician named, by title or part of it.

row.description: The row: its heading as printed, a number to find, or words of the heading.

table.description: The table: its number as printed ("Table 99") or words of its title.
